clue.text: Relatives around Peruvian city drink by old mountain

indicators.note: the relatives' word is placed round the city, enclosing it

parts.note: kin are one's relatives
Lima is the capital of Peru
a jar is British slang for a drink, especially of beer

explanation.surface: Family members round a Peruvian city have a drink beside an ancient peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals that the relatives enclose the city. A jar is everyday British slang for a pint in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is Africa's highest peak, an example of the defining word.

clue.text: Jumpers and anoraks go tatty

indicators.note: tatty means shabby and worn out, so these letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: Sweaters and waterproof jackets become scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumpers' looks like sweaters, the British word, beside anoraks; it is the hopping animals. 'tatty' signals the anagram of ANORAKS GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Kangaroos are marsupials that move by leaping, so they are literal jumpers.

clue.text: The French bank with good interior generally

parts.note: la is French for the

indicators.note: the good letter goes in the interior of the bank word, placed inside it

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A French bank with something good at its heart, broadly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a financial institution, but it is the verb in 'bank on'; 'interior' places the good letter just inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Largely means for the most part, mainly or in general.

clue.text: Explosives on lid covering opening of first access tunnel

parts.note: mines are explosive devices

indicators.note: the lid word covers the letter by enclosing it

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Explosive devices on a cover hiding the start of the first passage underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening of' takes one letter from 'first'; 'covering' wraps the lid synonym round it, giving HFAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineshaft is the vertical passage giving access to a mine's tunnels.

clue.text: Small creatures not before seen climbing stone

parts.note: something new has not been seen before

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Tiny animals never spotted before are scaling a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses ST to TS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Newts are small amphibians, examples of little animals.

clue.text: An upright member in charge is virtuous

indicators.note: in a down entry, set upright means the letters read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member

explanation.surface: A decent person in charge stands tall and is good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upright' reverses LEG to GEL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means saintly or exceptionally good in behaviour, hence morally pure.

clue.text: To do urgently — masking smell

indicators.note: the phrase masks the answer, concealing it within its letters

explanation.surface: An urgent task concealing a whiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masking' signals the answer concealed in tO DO URgently.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a scent, especially an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Figure trapped by discontented gangster is ill-fated person

indicators.note: the figure is caught inside what the gangster leaves, enclosed by it
with its contents gone, only the word's first and last letters remain

parts.note: one is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A character caught by a dissatisfied mobster is doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' is a pun: the gangster's contents, its middle letters, are emptied out; 'trapped by' puts the figure inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is informally someone doomed or beyond saving, an ill-fated individual.

clue.text: Becoming unfocused and idling in 50% of government

indicators.note: the idling word sits in the halved letters
half of the word, its first five of ten letters

parts.note: lazing is idling

explanation.surface: Losing concentration and loafing around within half the cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' keeps the first five of the ten letters of government; 'in' sets the idling word inside them, after the opening G.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes glazing over lose their focus, a sign of boredom or tiredness.

clue.text: Topical forum of different pug owners

indicators.note: a different arrangement of these letters is wanted, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: A discussion board for the various owners of pugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' signals the anagram of PUG OWNERS.
explanation.definitionFit: An online newsgroup is a discussion board dedicated to a particular subject or topic.

clue.text: Something delusional like high turnover?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for an unrealistic hope
a turnover is a kind of pastry pie, and one high up would be in the sky

explanation.surface: Something illusory, such as a dizzying business churn rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like business or staff churn; it is a folded pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie in the sky is an idiom for a fanciful hope unlikely to come true.

clue.text: Gaze exposed a meadow's flowers

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Look upon a field's open blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips Gaze to AZ; A, LEA and S follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Azaleas are flowering shrubs, so their blooms are examples of the plural defining word.

clue.text: Spend lots after place is overwhelmed by sudden increase

indicators.note: the place is swamped and so sits inside the sudden increase

parts.note: a surge is a sudden increase

explanation.surface: Splash out once a location is hit by a rush of demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is overwhelmed by' means the place abbreviation is engulfed, sitting inside the sudden increase; 'after' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to indulge in a burst of extravagant spending, spending lots in one go.

clue.text: Plant imbued with gold colour

indicators.note: something imbued with a thing has it inside, so the gold goes within the plant

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A plant infused with gold to give it a tint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbued with' puts the heraldic gold inside the plant; or is the heraldry word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is a creamy off-white shade named after elephant tusk material.

clue.text: Temperature within an office adjusted for warmth

indicators.note: the temperature letter goes inside the rearranged letters
adjusted means altered, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The thermostat in a workplace has been turned up for some heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' shuffles AN OFFICE to AFFECION; 'within' puts T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Affection is fond feeling, and warmth is a common figurative synonym for kindly regard.

clue.text: Designed shapes fit for soft foodstuff

indicators.note: designed means put together in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shapes fashioned to suit a mushy food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designed' signals the anagram of SHAPES FIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish paste is a smooth spread of ground fish, often used in British sandwiches.

clue.text: Uncle travelling with fine guide

indicators.note: letters on the move end up in a new order

explanation.surface: A relative on a journey with a good tour guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' signals the anagram of UNCLE + FINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To influence is to steer or shape, which is to guide, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Chat with rest in Ritz regularly about complaint

parts.note: gas is informal for idle chat

indicators.note: turning about means the following letters are read backwards

parts.note: to sit is to rest

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the words in Ritz

explanation.surface: Gossiping while relaxing in a grand London hotel leads to a grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks alternate letters from both words 'in Ritz', not Ritz alone; 'about' turns the rest synonym and that pick round together. The Ritz is a famous London luxury hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastritis, stomach-lining inflammation, is a medical complaint in the sense of an ailment.

clue.text: Cover sheltering mass inside of aula, as much as chamber holds

indicators.note: the cover shelters the mass by enclosing it

parts.note: a roof is a cover
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

indicators.note: the inside of a word is all but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A roof sheltering the people within a hall, filling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheltering' puts the mass abbreviation under the cover; 'inside of' drops the outer letters of aula, a Latin word for a hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A roomful is the amount or number a room can contain.

clue.text: Proportion of mud that's fine for lake

indicators.note: one thing given for another replaces it, so fine takes the place of lake

parts.note: filth, like mud, is dirt
L is an abbreviation for lake on maps
F is the pencil grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: How much of the mud is acceptable for a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the L in FILTH for F.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifth is one of five equal parts, a fraction or share of a whole.

clue.text: Fluster receiving bill raised for headwear

indicators.note: the fluster word receives the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a flap is a state of fluster

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a bill passed by parliament becomes an act

explanation.surface: Panicking on getting an invoice brings on a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses ACT to TCA; 'receiving' puts it in FLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat cap is a soft round cap with a short brim, associated with northern England.

clue.text: Long-winded poem about retired old boy

indicators.note: the poem goes round the reversed letters

parts.note: verse is poetry, a poem

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A rambling poem about a former pupil who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like stopping work but turns the old boy round; 'about' wraps the poem around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbose describes speech or writing using too many words, so it is wordy and long-winded.

clue.text: Routes heading off from East Anglian waterways

indicators.note: the head of the word, its first letter, comes off

parts.note: the Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in Norfolk and Suffolk, in East Anglia, eastern England

explanation.surface: Paths branching away from the waterways of eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the B from BROADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads are routes for traffic between places.

clue.text: We heard you advanced money for foreigners

indicators.note: what we heard is a sound-alike of the phrase

parts.note: you rose, meaning you went up or advanced

explanation.surface: We were told you lent cash to people from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You rose' said quickly matches EUROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Euros are the currency used across much of continental Europe, foreign money to a Briton.

clue.text: Signs a record returning with mission incomplete

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: left incomplete, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a quest is a mission

explanation.surface: Indicators of an album coming back from an unfinished assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns A LP into PLA; 'incomplete' trims QUEST to QUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaques are inscribed plates on walls, a kind of sign marking a place or person.

clue.text: Official protecting first-rate companies testifies again

indicators.note: the official shelters the grade letter by surrounding it

parts.note: a ref, or referee, is a sports official
A is the top grade, first-rate
firms are companies

explanation.surface: A referee shielding top businesses gives evidence a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts A inside REF, giving REAF.
explanation.definitionFit: To reaffirm is to declare or assert once more, which testifying again does.

clue.text: Sweet American characters either side of celebrity

wordplay.reading: C (first letter of celebrity) and Y (last letter)

parts.note: take the letters standing at either end of the word celebrity, then read the description itself aloud as a phrase

explanation.surface: A sugary treat from the US, with notable people on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of celebrity are C and Y; the phrase 'C and Y' itself is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the usual American word for what Britons call sweets.

clue.text: Lose apples diverted by European vendors

indicators.note: sent off course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Traders who mislay apples are distracted by a continental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' shuffles LOSE APPLES to SALESPEOPL; E ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Salespeople sell goods, so they are vendors.
